//: The bands below teach you to be reliable. This one teaches you to produce findings other people
can rely on, which is a different and harder thing: it requires being able to kill your own

modules.title: Hypothesis and refutation
modules.teaches: state a claim so precisely that a specific observation would destroy it, then go looking for that observation
modules.method: for every finding, write the sentence 'this is wrong if ___'. If you cannot complete it, the finding is not yet a claim. Then run the test that would complete it.
modules.exam: take a conclusion you believe, design the experiment most likely to refute it, run it, and report the result whichever way it falls

modules.title: Measurement
modules.teaches: measure the thing you are actually claiming, and earn a negative result with a wider probe than a positive one
modules.method: before reporting an absence, normalise both sides or key the comparison on something machine-stable. Before reporting a recovery, check the thing that recovered is the thing you care about - the first component back is the most misleading witness available.
modules.exam: produce a case where a plausible measurement answers a different question than the one being asked, and identify the correct probe

modules.title: Publication and review
modules.teaches: record work so it can be checked by a hostile reader, and survive being told you were wrong
modules.method: publish the evidence, not the conclusion alone. Cite what you read. Name what you did not check. Invite the strongest objection you can construct, and answer it in the record.
modules.exam: have a finding survive an adversarial review by someone trying to refute it - or be refuted, and record that outcome as carefully as a success

modules.title: Teaching
modules.teaches: convert your own scars into curriculum without handing anyone your injuries
modules.method: for each scar, ask what CAPABILITY it argues for. Teach that, and file the incident as evidence. A student who must memorise your history has been given knowledge, which rots; a student who gains the capability can meet a situation you never saw.
modules.exam: turn one of your own failures into a module with a real exam, where a reader who never had your failure still gains the ability
